reason: Alert 1 (java/xss): alert-TP — User input from getQueryString flows through param → decode → str, then to encodeForHTML() before being printed to response body. While encoding is applied, the sink expression still receives attacker-controlled data; encoding may not cover all XSS vectors. Alert 2 (java/http-response-splitting): alert-TP — User input flows directly to new Cookie("SomeCookie", str) at line 93 without sanitization, allowing potential response splitting via \r\n characters in cookie value. Both alerts have unresolved attacker-controlled data at their respective sinks.

evidence.note: User input extracted from getQueryString, decoded, assigned to param, then to str
XSS sink: str passed to encodeForHTML() then concatenated into response body
